DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

Letters You Can Hear

STS-MS6-L3-10001300-MSVPA-PPX-IMR-02 • MS Music Grades 6 to 8 • Performing with Technical Accuracy
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Every month this class mails sound letters across the ocean to a partner school. Each one holds a song a student learned from a grandparent who carried it across a border, written down by hand so a stranger far away can play it exactly the way it was meant to sound. The class rule is short: send it as the composer wrote it, so nothing gets lost on the trip.
If you mailed one song to someone far away, what would you write on the page so they played it the way you hear it in your head?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
Look at Yusra. What is Yusra doing?
Look at the picture. Say what Yusra is doing and why her eyes stay where they are. Speak in two complete sentences.
2
Look at Deniz. What is Deniz holding?
Look at the picture. Say what Deniz is holding and where he is putting it. Speak in two complete sentences.
3
Look at the teacher. What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Say what the teacher is doing and why this room needs it done. Speak in two complete sentences.
4
Where are these students? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Say where these students are and what evidence tells you. Speak in two complete sentences.
5
Tell me about the mail wall.
Look at the picture. Say what the wall holds and how it is organized. Speak in two complete sentences.
6
Look at Marisol. What is Marisol wearing?
Look at the picture. Say what Marisol is wearing and how it is different from what the others wear. Speak in two complete sentences.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: MU:Pr6.1.6a — Perform with technical accuracy to convey the creator’s intent. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
